sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *quisiera* and *me gustaría* from A2 Unit 26, where the conditional softens a request (*¿Podría ayudarme?*). You also know from B2 Unit 9 how *si* + imperfect subjunctive puts a request at a distance (*Si tuviera un momento…*). This lesson adds a different kind of *si* clause. It is not imagined: the condition is real, and the verb is in the present indicative. The speaker is checking a fact or asking permission while speaking, and the phrase makes the sentence sound careful and polite. Four useful ones are *si no me equivoco* "if I'm not mistaken", *si mal no recuerdo* "if I remember rightly", *si me permite* "if you will allow me" and *si no es molestia* "if it is no trouble". They can come at the start, in the middle or at the end of a sentence, and they are always set off with commas.

sections.title: Four polite phrases
rows: Si no me equivoco, la reunión es el jueves.
If I am not mistaken, the meeting is on Thursday. (checking a fact)
Si mal no recuerdo, empieza a las diez.
If I remember rightly, it starts at ten. (checking a memory)
Si me permite, quisiera hacer una pregunta.
If you will allow me, I would like to ask a question. (asking leave to speak)
Si no es molestia, ¿me lo podría enviar hoy?
If it is no trouble, could you send it to me today? (softening a request)

items.spanish: Usted, si no me equivoco, ya trabajó con nosotros.
items.english: You, if I am not mistaken, have already worked with us.

items.spanish: Si me permite, quisiera hacer una breve objeción.
items.english: If you will allow me, I would like to make a short objection.

items.spanish: Si no es molestia, ¿podría repetir la dirección?
items.english: If it is no trouble, could you repeat the address?

items.spanish: El plazo termina el viernes, si mal no recuerdo.
items.english: The deadline ends on Friday, if I remember rightly.

sections.content: With someone you call *usted*, say *si me permite* and *si no le importa*. With a friend, change the pronoun: *si me permites*, *si no te importa*. Keep these phrases in the present indicative, because they are real conditions. The imperfect subjunctive (*si fuera tan amable de…*) belongs to the more distant requests of B2 Unit 9. Write a comma before and after the phrase when it sits in the middle of a sentence.
